questions.title: Where sympathetic outflow originates
questions.question: From which specific regions of the central nervous system do the sympathetic nerves originally emerge?

options.D: The lower lumbar and sacral regions

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cranial nerve nuclei do contribute autonomic outflow, but that is the PARASYMPATHETIC (craniosacral) division, not the sympathetic one, and there is no distinct "cervical" autonomic outflow level.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cervical and sacral levels are not where sympathetic preganglionic neurons sit; the sacral cord contributes to the parasympathetic (craniosacral) division instead.
explanations.C: Correct. Sympathetic (thoracolumbar) outflow arises from preganglionic neurons in the lateral horn of the spinal cord grey matter across the thoracic and upper two lumbar segments (roughly T1-L2). Parasympathetic (craniosacral) outflow, by contrast, leaves from cranial nerve nuclei in the brainstem and from the second to fourth sacral spinal segments — the two divisions never share an outflow level.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lower lumbar and sacral segments are below the true sympathetic outflow range (which stops around L2) and are instead part of the parasympathetic (sacral) territory.

questions.learning_objective: State that sympathetic (thoracolumbar) outflow arises from thoracic and upper lumbar cord segments.
